sentences.text: In the year 1850, Clara was a young slave woman.
She lived on a large plantation in Georgia.
Her life was full of hard work and pain.
She dreamed of freedom every night.
One day, she decided to escape.
Clara knew about the Underground Railroad.
It was not just a secret path.
It was a real network of tunnels and trains.
She had heard stories from other slaves.
They said it could take her to the North, where she could be free.
One dark night, Clara made her move.
She ran through the fields, her heart pounding.
She reached the edge of the plantation and found a hidden entrance.
It was a small door covered by bushes.
She opened it and climbed down into the tunnel.
The tunnel was dark and cold.
Clara felt scared but determined.
She walked for hours, guided by a small lantern.
The walls were damp, and the air was thick.
She could hear the distant sound of a train.
It gave her hope.
After a long walk, Clara reached an underground station.
There were other escaped slaves there.
They looked tired but hopeful.
A man named Samuel was in charge.
He welcomed Clara and gave her food and water.
"You are safe here," Samuel said.
"But the journey is not over.
We must take the train to the next station."
Clara nodded.
She was ready to continue.
The train arrived, and they all got on.
It was an old, rusty train, but it was their ticket to freedom.
The train moved slowly through the tunnels.
Clara looked out the window.
She saw the walls of the tunnel passing by.
She felt a mix of fear and excitement.
The journey was long and dangerous.
At one point, the train had to stop.
There were guards searching for escaped slaves.
Samuel told everyone to be quiet.
Clara held her breath.
The guards passed by without noticing them.
The train started moving again.
Finally, after many hours, they reached the last station.
It was near the border of a free state.
Clara could hardly believe it.
She climbed out of the tunnel and saw the open sky.
She was free at last.
Clara thanked Samuel and the others.
She knew she had a long way to go, but she was no longer a slave.
She could start a new life.
She walked towards the North, feeling the sun on her face.
She was ready for whatever came next.
